meta.move: Strong path to agreement with a deadline said aloud
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm here. You asked for twenty minutes, so I'll take them. Who decided on the zero, Hale, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?
I owe you an apology: I put the zero in before calling you. That was my mistake.
Okay. And Owen found out from the gradebook, on his phone, in the middle of class. What do you have, Hale?
On November 2 I asked Owen what 'epistemological paralysis' means. He said 'like, being stuck', and he couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that down the same day.

I'm writing down November 2, Hale. "Like, being stuck" is a seventeen-year-old answering a vocabulary question on the spot, and that doesn't tell me who wrote the essay. The note you made that day, is it dated, and can I see it?
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay never mentions cowardice.

Students change their argument between an outline and a final draft, Hale; it's called revising. Is the outline dated October 15 in front of you, and does it say "cowardice" in Owen's own words? Turn the screen, or put the page on the desk.
Here's my offer: a supervised rewrite, Thursday at 8:15 in my room. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll send you that in writing by Friday at 3 PM.

That's procedure 4.4, Hale, so you're offering what your own policy already requires, and you still haven't put the outline or your note in front of me. The zero comes off the gradebook today while the rewrite is pending. Who decides whether it "holds up," and is it just Owen in the room?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require the zero withdrawn from the gradebook, the October 15 outline and your dated note from November 2 produced to me, and answers on who decides whether the rewrite holds up and who is in the room. I expect your written offer by Friday at 3 PM.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: opening position, with the zero still standing and nothing agreed.
What moved her: "I put the zero in before calling you", because owning it in one sentence earned a small sign of ground.
What cost ground: nothing.
Try next time: after you said the essay never mentions cowardice, put the dated outline and your note in front of her before you made the rewrite offer.
